pages.text: Melting snow swelled the spring stream. Fluffy willow catkins bloomed on the other bank.
Nils wanted to pick catkins for Grandpa's vase. Five stepping stones crossed the stream.
He stood before the first stone. Water roared beside it. "What if it wobbles...?" His foot wouldn't move.
Nils walked upstream. He would find a narrow spot and hop across.
Around the corner, the stream was even wider. His shoulders drooped.
Nils was back at the stones. The sun already rested on the treetops.
Across the water, catkins swayed in the wind. Only his toes wriggled. He still hadn't taken one step.
Grandpa stood on the first stone and stamped both feet. Thump, thump! It didn't budge.
Nils pressed his foot firmly on it. Steady! Even with loud water, the stone was strong.
Across! Nils picked catkins. From the other side of the stream, Grandpa clapped.
